I see you're experiencing a chronic cough and shortness of breath; to better understand what's going on, how long has this cough been persisting, and does it produce any phlegm or blood? Also, have you noticed any fever, weight loss, or night sweats recently?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation of the lungs, flattened diaphragms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the hyperinflation and flattened diaphragms suggest air trapping. Have you noticed a history of smoking, or do you experience wheezing and chest tightness, especially with cold air or exercise? How much does your shortness of breath limit your daily activities, such as climbing stairs?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I've been smoking a pack a day for twenty years, and I do notice my chest feels tight and whistling when I breathe in cold air or push myself on the job. My shortness of breath is really limiting me, as I can barely climb a single flight of stairs without stopping to catch my breath. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of heavy smoking combined with wheezing and significant exertional dyspnea is highly concerning for emphysema, though we must rule out cardiac causes. Since we cannot use an ECG or labs, please tell me if you ever wake up at night gasping for air (paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea) or if you have noticed swelling in your ankles? Also, does your cough produce any mucus, or is it dry?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't wake up gasping for air at night, and my ankles aren't swollen. My cough is definitely productive, though it's just white phlegm and not blood. I want to emphasize that, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), specifically Emphysema.
